This tutorial covers the science of complex systems: systems of many interacting parts whose collective behaviour is
not written into any one part. It starts with what makes a system complex and with the two engines of complexity,
nonlinear dynamics and randomness. It moves through fractals and scaling, phase transitions, cellular automata, pattern
formation, networks and the processes that spread on them, self-organized criticality, synchronization, collective
motion, agent-based models and evolution. It ends with information and complexity measures, tipping points, and the
reconstruction of dynamics and equations from data.

Each chapter sets out definitions and results, works through examples, and gives exercises to try. Every example and
solution is computed with scikit-complexity, so each model can be run and changed rather than only read. The
mathematics comes from
[Fundamentals of Mathematics for Physicists](../fundamentals-of-mathematics-for-physicists/index.qmd). Results of
statistical physics, such as Landau theory, mean field and the Langevin equation, are stated in
[Fundamentals of Theoretical Physics](../fundamentals-of-theoretical-physics/index.qmd), and the chapters link there
instead of repeating them.

::: {.start-reading}
The chapters are listed in reading order in the sidebar, followed by the [glossary](glossary/index.qmd). [Start with the notation →](notation/index.qmd)
:::

## Prerequisites

The chapters assume calculus and the following chapters of the other tutorials, and link to them where a result is
used:

- [Linear algebra](../fundamentals-of-mathematics-for-physicists/linear-algebra/index.qmd): eigenvalues, for
  stability, network spectra and synchronization.
- [Differential equations](../fundamentals-of-mathematics-for-physicists/differential-equations/index.qmd): flows,
  linear systems and the diffusion equation, for dynamics and pattern formation.
- [Probability](../fundamentals-of-mathematics-for-physicists/probability/index.qmd): random variables, limit theorems
  and estimation, for random processes, scaling and statistics.
- [Thermodynamics and statistical mechanics](../fundamentals-of-theoretical-physics/thermodynamics-statistical-mechanics/index.qmd):
  ensembles, entropy and Landau theory, for phase transitions and criticality.

## Software

The computations of every chapter use [scikit-complexity](https://pypi.org/project/scikit-complexity/) 0.9.0, pinned
to that version. It builds the models of the tutorial from a catalogue of ready-made systems, runs them with one
simulation engine, and analyses the results: Lyapunov exponents, fractal dimensions, entropies, network measures and
scaling laws. The recorded outputs on the pages come from that version.

Main library:

- [scikit-complexity](https://pypi.org/project/scikit-complexity/) 0.9.0: complex systems as scikit-learn-style
  estimators, with a catalogue of systems by field and topic, simulation experiments and analysis functions.

Other libraries, used for what scikit-complexity does not provide:

- [NumPy](https://numpy.org) and [SciPy](https://scipy.org): arrays, linear algebra and numerical methods.
- [NetworkX](https://networkx.org): graphs, their measures and algorithms.
- [Mesa](https://mesa.readthedocs.io): agent-based models written by hand.
- [powerlaw](https://github.com/jeffalstott/powerlaw): fitting and testing heavy-tailed distributions.

All of them are installed, at the versions the pages were computed with, by one command run from the root of the
[repository](https://github.com/georgedouzas/tutorials) (Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) required):

```bash
uv venv --python 3.12 .venv-complexity && uv pip install --python .venv-complexity/bin/python -r complexity-science/requirements.lock
```

This tutorial has its own [glossary](glossary/index.qmd).
